title: Trees and Binary Search Trees

steps.title: Tree vocabulary
steps.content: A tree is a hierarchical data structure. The top node is the root. A node may have children; a node with no children is a leaf. The path length counts edges between nodes.
steps.example: In a family tree, the top ancestor is the root and people with no listed children are leaves.

steps.title: Count children
steps.prompt: In a binary tree, what is the maximum number of children a node can have?
steps.explanation: A binary tree node has at most two children: left and right.

steps.title: Binary search tree order
steps.content: In a binary search tree, keys in the left subtree are smaller than the node's key, and keys in the right subtree are larger (assuming unique keys). This supports ordered searching.
steps.example: For root 8, value 3 belongs left and value 12 belongs right.
steps.tip: The ordering rule applies to the entire left and right subtrees, not just direct children.

steps.title: Recognize inorder traversal
steps.prompt: What is the usual output of inorder traversal of a binary search tree with unique keys?
steps.explanation: Inorder visits left subtree, node, then right subtree, producing ascending key order in a BST.

steps.title: Traversal methods
steps.content: Preorder visits node-left-right. Inorder visits left-node-right. Postorder visits left-right-node. Level order visits nodes breadth-first, usually using a queue.

questions.prompt: A node with no children is called a:
questions.explanation: A leaf node has no children.

questions.prompt: At which positions can a binary tree node have children?
questions.explanation: A binary tree allows at most a left child and a right child.

questions.prompt: Inorder traversal visits nodes in which order?
questions.explanation: Inorder is left subtree, node, right subtree.

questions.prompt: Which traversal is naturally implemented using a queue?
questions.explanation: Breadth-first level-order traversal uses a queue.

questions.prompt: In a BST, where does a value smaller than the current node belong?
questions.explanation: Smaller keys belong in the left subtree.

learning_objectives: Explain root, child, parent, leaf and height.
Trace preorder, inorder and postorder traversals.
Use a queue for level-order traversal.
Distinguish a general binary tree from a BST.

common_misconceptions.misconception: Every binary tree is a binary search tree.
common_misconceptions.correction: A BST additionally enforces an ordering rule on left and right subtrees.

common_misconceptions.misconception: Tree height and depth are the same for every node.
common_misconceptions.correction: Depth is measured from the root; height is measured down to a deepest leaf.

common_misconceptions.misconception: Inorder traversal sorts every binary tree.
common_misconceptions.correction: Inorder traversal is sorted only when the tree satisfies BST ordering.

worked_examples.title: Preorder traversal
worked_examples.explanation: Preorder order is root, left, right.

worked_examples.title: Inorder traversal
worked_examples.explanation: Inorder is left, root, right; this is sorted for a BST.

worked_examples.title: Level-order traversal
worked_examples.explanation: A queue visits nodes level by level.

company_applications.practice: Trace recursive calls and return order.
Compare DFS traversals with BFS level order.
Handle empty trees, one node and skewed trees.
